title: Randomized evaluation of volunteers relaying AI-based flood forecasts and alerts in Bihar, India (2022–2025 monsoons)
summary: In a Bihar trial, volunteers relayed Google and Central Water Commission flood alerts, and treated households under severe flooding were 12.7 percentage points less likely to have their home flooded.
account: Google's AI flood-forecasting system, run with India's Central Water Commission, issues riverine flood alerts as Android push notifications. In Bihar, India, the economists Maulik Jagnani (Tufts) and Rohini Pande (Yale) ran a randomized evaluation across 319 panchayats, or village councils, in 12 flood-prone districts. The non-governmental organization Yuganter trained community volunteers to relay the alerts in the treatment villages. Control villages received the same forecasts and alerts but had no volunteers. A working paper of 3 April 2024 covers the 2022 and 2023 monsoon seasons (June to October). The authors report that treatment households got 2.41 more alerts in 2022 and were 46.5% more likely to get an alert before water reached their area. In 2023 treatment households received 4.35 more alerts and were 88% more likely to receive an alert before water reached their panchayat. Treatment households reported 16.56% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical spending than controls. The authors report that households in treatment areas spent roughly INR 6,500 less on illness treatment, a 32.87% decrease. No specific evacuation tied to an alert is documented. A September 2026 version of the working paper covers four monsoon seasons from 2022 to 2025. The authors state that Google alerts were unavailable in 2022, when volunteers relayed Central Water Commission forecasts. From 2023 the volunteers relayed Google Flood Hub alerts and Google's flood maps. The authors state that the experiment isolates the value of community delivery. They state that it does not measure the value of the forecasting systems. Among control households under severe flooding, the chance of home flooding was 23.7 percentage points higher than in a season with no flood. The authors report that treated households under severe flooding were 12.7 percentage points less likely to have their own home flooded and borrowed about INR 12,600 less. They report that welfare gains concentrate in flooded villages, where the program raised a post-flood welfare index by 0.3 standard deviations. They also report gains in food security. They report that the program had no effect on physical health. This version does not repeat the illness and medical spending results of April 2024. The authors acknowledge financial support from Google.org.
purpose: The forecasting system was built to warn people of riverine floods before water arrives so that they can prepare or evacuate. The study measured the effects of relaying those warnings across groups of households.

fields.summary: In a Bihar trial, volunteers relayed Google and Central Water Commission flood alerts, and treated households under severe flooding were 12.7 percentage points less likely to have their home flooded.
fields.account: Google's AI flood-forecasting system, run with India's Central Water Commission, issues riverine flood alerts as Android push notifications. In Bihar, India, the economists Maulik Jagnani (Tufts) and Rohini Pande (Yale) ran a randomized evaluation across 319 panchayats, or village councils, in 12 flood-prone districts. The non-governmental organization Yuganter trained community volunteers to relay the alerts in the treatment villages. Control villages received the same forecasts and alerts but had no volunteers. A working paper of 3 April 2024 covers the 2022 and 2023 monsoon seasons (June to October). The authors report that treatment households got 2.41 more alerts in 2022 and were 46.5% more likely to get an alert before water reached their area. In 2023 treatment households received 4.35 more alerts and were 88% more likely to receive an alert before water reached their panchayat. Treatment households reported 16.56% fewer illness symptoms and about 30% lower medical spending than controls. The authors report that households in treatment areas spent roughly INR 6,500 less on illness treatment, a 32.87% decrease. No specific evacuation tied to an alert is documented. A September 2026 version of the working paper covers four monsoon seasons from 2022 to 2025. The authors state that Google alerts were unavailable in 2022, when volunteers relayed Central Water Commission forecasts. From 2023 the volunteers relayed Google Flood Hub alerts and Google's flood maps. The authors state that the experiment isolates the value of community delivery. They state that it does not measure the value of the forecasting systems. Among control households under severe flooding, the chance of home flooding was 23.7 percentage points higher than in a season with no flood. The authors report that treated households under severe flooding were 12.7 percentage points less likely to have their own home flooded and borrowed about INR 12,600 less. They report that welfare gains concentrate in flooded villages, where the program raised a post-flood welfare index by 0.3 standard deviations. They also report gains in food security. They report that the program had no effect on physical health. This version does not repeat the illness and medical spending results of April 2024. The authors acknowledge financial support from Google.org.
